comments.value: Currently as-is, green does not make much sense to me as to why it is in the game. If I am switching from orange to green, why not just change to blue? I really want to be able to see before-hand who wants to join off me, but I also want people to be able to know where I am. Sure if I am in a large gathering somebody I may wanted to have curated might join off another person, but a situation like that wouldn't always be the case.

Functionally I'm not even sure if blue/green has a difference, and if they're supposed to it doesn't work. I used to always be on orange because I "want people to knock" but I still want to seem open to people actually being there. I just don't like surprises. "Why are they on your friends list if you don't want them there?" I get asked a lot. Do people not have different friend groups for different social settings and personalitities IRL? Let people see where I am so they can decided if it's worth knocking, and let me open the door, please!

This 100%. Currently green is only useful if you hop instances a ton so you don't have to juggle between blue and orange in case you end up in a private instance. Would much prefer this to combat the problem of half the friends list permanently being on orange.

@{609a1fc2eeec070e82894e8d|full_name}: Difference between blue and green is that green is following world behavior, if you are in a private world, then green becomes that people need to request and so you will be notified, if you are on blue, the request will be automatically accepted and you’ll be joined without being notified yourself

@{62def40fd302ec44c0aaec2d|full_name}: At what point does the world become "private" though? I'm almost exclusively in Friends+ worlds, on green, and I find that I never need to accept requests; people can just join on me (functionally making it the same as blue). If I'm in Invite+ worlds, people have to send requests regardless. So is green only functionally significant in Friends worlds? That doesn't seem like how it should work. Or are we all using worlds wrong?

@{609a1fc2eeec070e82894e8d|full_name}: No, in invite+ people have to send request, but on blue, it will be accepted and you won’t be notified as if it was friends+, than on green as I said, it follows instance types.

Green and Blue are the same in Public and Friends+ and Friends as these worlds are open anyway to your friends

They act different in invite and invite+ where on blue, your friends can still join you no matter what (as instance creator for invite ofc) 

Orange and Green are different, as said, Green follow instance rule and show Public world you are in; Orange is when you want everything hidden and need peeps to request.

So no blue is not green, and yes green is working as intended meaning « available following instance type »

What you guys ask for is different; from what I get of the original post at least, is to have another status mixing the fact that people need to request all the time like orange, but can see the instance you are in as long as it is public like green

So like a yellow status

But green works fine and as it always did and was intended to imo, i like the way things works rn and if I am in private I don’t feel the need that peeps just see the name of the world I am in

But again just my opinion

I will also add, if you want to be green just for some specific peeps that can join you anytime and don’t want to be joined by others, that is why groups were made
Yes!! As _Leucis_ mentioned, this is exactly why most people are set to orange. I agree that if this suggestion is how green worked I would use it waaaayy more often.

@{62def40fd302ec44c0aaec2d|full_name}: Thank you so much for explaining! I genuinely didn't understand because I almost never use anything above Friends+. 

I can understand why you like the way things are now but I personally disagree. The vast majority of instances used in VRC, in my experience, are Public and Friends+. If 3/5 instance types (two of them being the most popular) render two status colors the same, they're functionally redundant in those instance types and can be improved upon. Green should act the way it does in Invite and Invite+, just with the addition that you can see the world (which I feel is basically what this post is suggesting if I'm reading it correctly). Private worlds (Invite and Invite+) would still be private, no matter what color you're on.

Locking the functionality of curating who we choose to join us anytime to group-only instances when making them is a VRC+ feature is both clunky and unfair. It's also not the same functionality this is asking for; anyone outside a group can't see where you are. Group instances seem work best for specific purposes (like a D&D group) and large-scale events.

At the very least, maybe there /should/ be an in-between yellow status.

So much support for this. I'm always on orange because I want to be able to control who joins the instance. Some friends don't vibe with other friends, sometimes I only want to hang out with certain people, there's plenty of reasons for it. But there's almost never a reason for me to hide where I am and make people think I'm totally "off limits" for joining, I just want to be able to decline certain people if I need to.

I'm not sure if replacing the current green status is the best way of going about it though, there is some value in having an "auto accept if I'm in public/friends worlds but curate if I'm in a private world" setting. A new status entirely would be the best of both worlds
@{5e828313c5f5e9204b146fc3|full_name}: A new status entirely would be a good solution too, agreed
Pretty good, but would prefer a fifth status, such as yellow for this

It's funny because when I read how the statuses worked, I had assumed that green works like this *already*, but it doesn't. If someone is in Friends, Friends+, or Public, it allows them to auto-join.

I wouldn't mind being on green to show friends where I am, but I also would prefer to have the option to invite, at least if I already can invite people. 

For example, the current functionality of Invite+ is that other users can only invite if they are requested on (I think this is silly, but I digress). It would be helpful to show people that I am in an Invite+ world so they know to request on me.

And to recap on that Invite+ thing: I just wish that we were allowed to have more granular control over the instance settings, rather than having these instance types. I really do think Invite+ should be: anyone can invite, but no one can auto-join, since that's what I assumed it should do.

@{63ac3213dc63a1456881413d|full_name}: Agreed, I'm on green most of the time because I like the default behavior (anyone can join in friends+ without me having to accept a request, more-private instances get routed to me with a request).

Admittedly I'd go blue more often if I could create instances (including my home world) that are for only me with no invites, mostly because if I'm checking out worlds and didn't join the public then usually I don't necessarily want someone joining in without knocking first.

A year later and I'm still wishing this was implemented. So many people don't request on me because I'm on Orange. I want to be able to go on Green without my friend groups colliding, causing drama, and me losing friends.

It's amazing idea and I wish we had that

However there's an issue

For Friends+ or Friends, if the user that is trying to join you, know the World and Instance ID, they can bypass requesting invite off of you by just finding that world, going into instance list and joining through there, completely bypassing any request to invite etc..

I wanna add in my two cents. for this.

I am likely one of several people who don't like surprise friend visits the moment I've loaded into VRC, and for me, I like to think of my desire to socialize like an old Windows XP laptop: Slow to boot, but once fully booted, everything runs smoothly until the battery dies.

That being said, when I'm not "fully booted," I will not be interested in my friends just showing up in my instance and bee-lining straight to me, as that can drain my battery sooner than I'd like.

So I use Orange. And get no Invites/Requests 'cause Orange might as well be Do Not Disturb.

But if I use Green, I suddenly have people showing up and instantly wanting to hang out when I've not got the energy just yet, or am even in a map that would be bad for them to join, like Pop Escape [late joiner unfriendly] or No Time Two Talk [unable to se other people until you're matched, and might not be my friend whom I'm matched with].

Not to mention that there was a bug once that made Notifs just fail to show up in game, so even if Sandra Dean or whoever wanted to join me, I could very well just never get the notif 'cause this bug hasn't been fixed/patched out, as far as I'm aware.

Yeah, I could also change what my status says, but do people other than me actually read those things often enough to make doing so viable? 

Longform short: Orange is too strict for my friends, but Green is too lax for me, and I just want a way that guides people to send Requests/Invites instead of just joining off of me, but also doesn't scare people off from even trying to send any at all, which is what happens given the way things are now.

details:
This change would make the statuses break down very cleanly:

- Show world, auto-accept joins (current blue)

- Show world, curate who joins (my new green)

- Hide world, curate who joins (current orange)

- Hide world, no joins (current red)

How private you want your hangout to be can change throughout the course of a single conversation. Sometimes you're having a very casual hang and then you get into a serious topic, and might not want people joining during it. Social behavior is fluid and changing status mid-conversation is unnatural and cumbersome.

This green status change would give a "door's open, but you still gotta knock" option, where you're generally open to people joining, but you still want to be able to exercise discretion about who joins and exactly when as the need arises. Orange feels much too private for casual hangouts, but you don't always want ANYBODY to join ALWAYS. Personally if this were implemented, I'd be on it all the time.
title: Update the Green status to have the exact same behavior as orange, but with your world shown.
